card.name: Bhagavata Mela
card.era: 16th century (after the fall of Vijayanagara, c. 1565)
card.tagline: Tamil Nadu's Vaishnava temple dance-drama of Melattur
card.profile: Bhagavata Mela is a classical dance-drama tradition of Tamil Nadu, especially Melattur near Thanjavur, performed as an annual Vaishnavite temple offering, primarily to Lord Lakshmi Narasimha (Wikipedia). It descends from Kuchipudi: after the fall of the Vijayanagara Empire (~1565), some Telugu Brahmin dance-drama families migrated south and were granted land by king Achuthappa Nayak, evolving the Kuchipudi-inspired form into Bhagavata Mela. Traditionally enacted entirely by male Brahmins (including female roles), beginning after dusk by oil lamps, it combines Nritta, Nritya and Natya set to Carnatic music, drawing on the Natya Shastra (Wikipedia; Melattur Bhagavata Mela).
card.insight: Its core repertoire is the ten Telugu dance-dramas of Melattur Venkatarama Sastri (1743-1809), of which 'Prahlada Charitram', performed on Narasimha Jayanti, is the most enduring (DT Next; The Verandah Club).
